To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the asymptotic behavior of the minimal speed is expressed in terms of variational quantities and that the positivity of the limit is characterized in terms of a condition on the advection field.

the minimal speed of a pulsating traveling front for the reaction-advection-differential equation within a periodic heterogeneous environment is asymptotically equivalent, up to an exponentially small error, to the maximum of a certain variational quantity over the family of first integrals of the advection vector field, and that the limit is positive if and only if the advection vector is not tangent to a level set of the first integral at any point.
the speed of propagation of KPP reaction-difference equations within a large drift is asymptotically given by the maximum of certain variational quantity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the minimal speed $c^{\ast}(\lambda,\mu)$ of pulsating fronts in the Fisher-KPP equation $$ u_t=\lambda u_{xx}+ \mu u_x+u(1-u), $$ where the parameter $0<\lambda\ll1$ is the ratio of the diffusion coefficient to the advection one, $\mu\in\R$ is the advection coefficient and $u$ is defined on $\R\times \T$ and is
the study of the speed of propagation of the KPP fronts within a drift.
the study of the speed of propagation for the KPP reaction-difusion equation within either an advective term, a large diffusion term or a mixture of both.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in any space dimension, the asymptotics for the minimal speed is given by a variational formula which involves the family of first integrals of the advection vector field and that the positivity of the minimal speed is characterized in dimension 2.

in any dimension $N,$ if the advection field is a gradient vector field then the minimal speed of pulsating fronts is asymptotically linear in the drift parameter and if it is not, then there exists a drift value above which the minimal speed is asymptotically constant.
the minimal speed of pulsating traveling front is asymptotically given by the maximum of the first integrals of the drift.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the minimal speed of pulsating traveling front is the maximum over the set of first integrals of the drift of the minimal speeds of propagation of the Fisher-KPP equation within the same drift and a small reaction.

the minimal speed of pulsating fronts is asymptotically equivalent to the minimal speed of the corresponding advection field within a large drift and the reaction term only affects the minimal speed in a very small range of drift.
the minimal speed within either a large diffusion or a mixture of a large diffusion and a small reaction converges to the minimal speed within the advection equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the minimal speed of the KPP reaction-difussion equation is not a continuous function of the advection term.
the asymptotic behavior of the minimal speed is governed by a competition between the drift and the reaction/diffusion.
the speed of propagation is not affected by the drift if and only if the advection field is divergence-free.
